summary: Hillsborough County steel fire tower built in 1937, saved in 1993 and now a county park landmark; the 1936 date and 85 ft height are secondhand.

facts.design: Steel fire lookout tower; the Eastern lookout listing says a steel tower was erected in 1937
facts.agency: Hillsborough County (formerly the Florida Division of Forestry)

access.note: Part of Hamner Tower Park, a county park on North Boulevard with an open field and a hiking trail. The county page does not say whether the tower itself can be climbed.

visit.trail_note: Open field and hiking trail in the county park; parking runs along North Boulevard.

events.note: Built 1937 per NHLR; the Eastern lookout listing also gives 1937. A blog quoting a Water Atlas document gives 1936.
Ruth Foster listed as towerwoman in a November 13, 1950 list of observation towers
Tower saved from demolition when county commissioners voted to buy the property from the state
Designated a Hillsborough County historic landmark
Registered March 14, 2014 as US 996, FL 5; nominated by Sheryl Bowman

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, the Eastern lookout listing and the Tampa Bay Times give 1937. A blog post quoting a Water Atlas document gives 1936. The Water Atlas PDF was not opened, so 1937 is used and 1936 is recorded as a secondhand report.

notes_for_editor: Height (85 ft, 25.9 m) and the 1936 date come only from a blog quoting a Water Atlas PDF that was not opened; verify before publishing a stronger claim. NHLR's '52 ft (16 m)' is labeled Elevation, so it is ground elevation, and the brief's elevation_m 15.8 is that figure. Climbing status of the tower is not documented. Page reads: 7 (one over the cap), because some pages were re-read to get full text.
